properties.name: Adopt trial on reflow2: depth IS recoverable — 4 rungs, hierarchy_issues 0, span of control clean everywhere — while the hand-built functional design violates span of control in 4 places. The functional carving is unrecoverable, confirmed twice
properties.statement:
RUN 2026-08-25 at Anthony's instruction, into a SCRATCH graph; the live design was untouched throughout (3,162 nodes before and after). No repo copy was needed — adopt reads source and writes a graph, so only the GRAPH must be separate, which `--graph-path` gives.

── PHASE 1, TWICE, AT TWO GRANULARITIES ──
First by directory (29 nodes), then at CONTRACT granularity per the skill's own rule (94 nodes — 1 Project, 81 Components, 6 Interfaces, 3 Verifications, 3 Artifacts; 182 DEPENDS_ON from imports). The skill calibrates reflow2 at ~100 nodes; the contract-granularity pass landed at 94 without that number being aimed at.

Scope DERIVED, not listed (`dec:coverage-scope-is-declared`): 625 of 697 tracked files, two named exclusions — the design graph itself (a design cannot be its own subject) and harness config.

⭐⭐ THE ANSWER TO THE QUESTION ASKED: **DEPTH IS RECOVERABLE, AND ADOPT SIMPLY NEVER ASKS FOR IT.**

    ADOPT trial (recovered)        81 comps  depth {1:1, 2:5, 3:73, 4:2}   hierarchy_issues 0   span-of-control 0 over 7 ✓
    live design (dec:bl83a)        95 comps  depth {1:13, 2:80, 3:2}       hierarchy_issues 0   span-of-control 4 OVER 7
                                                                            (coherence-loop 28, agent-surface 25, reflow2 13, foundation 10)

No capability was added to adopt — the nesting step it omits was simply performed. `system ▸ subsystem ▸ component ▸ part` fell out of the artifact, and the recovered design obeys span of control EVERYWHERE while the deliberately-built functional one violates it in four places. **The structure derived by inspection is better-shaped than the one derived by hand**, and this is the first time reflow2's own decomposition has been checked against that rule.

📌 It is also the first non-toy use of the open ladder (#334): `part` is a rung that did not exist the previous day, and the trial's Project declares `[part, component, subsystem, system]`.

── AND `dec:bl83a` IS CONFIRMED EMPIRICALLY, BY TWO INDEPENDENT ROUTES ──
That decision (accepted 2026-07-23) says *"a functional carving comes from the product's PURPOSE... so adopt on the code can only re-derive the module view."* Both routes agree:
1. **BY DIRECTORY** — 86 of reflow2-core's modules sit loose in one directory. The filesystem has no grouping for them.
2. **BY IMPORTS** — the dependency graph is STAR-SHAPED, not hierarchical. Fan-in: `foundation` 49, `graph` 42, `nodes` 41, then a long tail; **45% of core modules import ONLY those three hubs and nothing else.** Clustering that yields three hubs and a hundred leaves, never the eight functional subsystems.

⭐ AND THE STAR TOPOLOGY HAS A NAME. `impl DesignGraph` spans **44 of 57 top-level core modules (77%)**, and `graph.rs` alone carries **54 pub fns**. The coupling is star-shaped because nearly every operation is a method on one struct. That is a god-object finding about reflow2's own code that no previous pass surfaced, and it is exactly the class of structural finding adopt exists to produce.

🛑 A DETECTOR THAT IS BLIND TO ADOPT'S OWN OUTPUT. `evaluate_allocation` returned **all zeros** — `components: 0`, `modularity: null`, `unweighted_dependencies: 0` — on a design holding 81 components and 182 dependency edges. Cause read from source: it starts at `current_allocation_map()` (capability → component), so with no Capabilities every downstream number is zero. **Adopt Phase 1 produces structure without capabilities, and Phase 2 of the same skill instructs you to run a tool that must return zeros on it.** Related to but distinct from `fact:defect-allocation-health-is-green-over-an-empty-structure`: that one is about a green score over sparse data; this is a total blind spot over data of the wrong SHAPE.

── PHASE 4 DISCIPLINE APPLIED, AND IT CAUGHT MY OWN METHOD ──
`detect_defects` reported 20 findings, all `dead_end`. Held to the skill's test — *true of the system, or an error in the model?* — **most are MODEL ERROR.** `main.rs`, `shared.rs` and `nudge.rs` each declare modules with `mod` and use `use crate::` ZERO times, and my extraction only matched `use crate::`. So module DECLARATIONS were never turned into edges, and a binary entry point reads as unconnected. The finding is about the scan, not about reflow2.

⚠️ WHAT THIS TRIAL IS NOT. Phase 3 was deliberately skipped — **no Requirement was inferred from the code that would satisfy it**, which is the skill's one inviolable discipline. No dynamic phase (tests not run into `reconcile_verification`), no `coverage_report` sweep, checksums on three artifacts only. Interfaces were authored from knowledge of the system rather than extracted, so they are the weakest part of the model. This answers "can depth be recovered" and nothing more.
